item.title: On the minimality of the compact right-angled 120-cell
item.description: arXiv:2610.33053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a compact right-angled polytope in hyperbolic 4-space has at least 120 facets, with equality only for the right-angled 120-cell. This answers a question of Potyagailo and Vinberg. As a consequence, the right-angled 120-cell is the unique compact right-angled 4-polytope of minimal volume and f-vector.
item.dc:creator: Lizi Guo, Fangting Zheng

item.title: On the Upsilon invariant and the Baldwin-Vela-Vick b-invariant of fibered knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.33280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a null-homologous fibered knot $K$ in a rational homology sphere, Baldwin and Vela-Vick define a refinement $b(K)$ of the Ozsv\'ath-Szab\'o contact invariant. We prove that if the Ozsv\'ath-Stipsicz-Szab\'o concordance invariant Upsilon has slope $\Upsilon'_K(t)=-g(K)$ for some $t\in[0,\frac{2}{n+1})$, where $g(K)$ is the genus of $K$, then $b(K)>n$. This extends a result of He, Hubbard, and the author on the Upsilon invariant and right-veering monodromies. We also prove that the knot Floer homology of a fibered knot in the $g(K)-b(K)$ Alexander grading is nonvanishing. As an application, we give many families of fibered cable knots whose $b(K)$ invariant grows arbitrarily large. Finally, we prove that if a monodromy of a fibered knot is neither right-veering nor left-veering, then the third-to-top term of knot Floer homology is nonvanishing.
item.dc:creator: Linh Truong

item.title: Delambre--Gauss Formulas in Complex Hyperbolic Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.33468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Delambre--Gauss matrix identity for oriented right-angled hexagons in the complex hyperbolic plane. The six complex length parameters of a hexagon determine two alternating \(3\times3\) matrices whose product is central in (\mathrm{SU}(2,1)\). The resulting nine entry-wise equations extend the Delambre-Gauss formula of Tan, Wong, and Zhang in 4-dimensional hyperbolic geometry to this complex hyperbolic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiming Ma, Baohua Xie

item.title: Dancing circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.33867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent results on diffeomorphisms of $4$-manifolds make essential use of families of embeddings of $1$-manifolds into $4$-manifolds. We survey what is currently known about such families.
item.dc:creator: Danica Kosanovi\'c

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay

item.title: Contact 3-manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings
item.description: arXiv:2610.34381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct the first examples of contact $3$-manifolds admitting infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings which are rational homology balls. Our examples are planar. They are obtained by a simple modification of Baykur's recent planar contact $3$-manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings, and the fillings are distinguished by their fundamental groups. For one of these rational homology balls we give an explicit Kirby diagram, with a single $1$-handle and a single $2$-handle attached along a trefoil, which exhibits its boundary as $(0,-8)$-surgery on a two-component link. We also identify the smooth topology of Baykur's example: $Y$ is obtained by $(0,-8)$-surgery on the link $7^2_4$, and it is Seifert fibered over the Klein bottle with one exceptional fiber. Finally, we construct further Stein fillings of $(Y,\xi)$, which realize all the groups $\mathbb Z/m\rtimes_{-1}\mathbb Z$, $m\ge0$, as their fundamental groups.
item.dc:creator: Burak Ozbagci

item.title: On Khovanov homology of virtual links
item.description: arXiv:2610.34438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Khovanov homology of virtual knots defined by V.O. Manturov and the Khovanov homology defined by D. Tubbenhauer coincide.
item.dc:creator: Igor Nikonov

item.title: Positivity of simplicial volume and uniqueness for the twelve-vertex flag three-spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.34743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the twelve-vertex flag triangulation $T_{12}$ of $S^3$ and the Davis $4$-manifold $M(T_{12})$ associated with it. We prove that $T_{12}$ is, up to isomorphism, the unique flag triangulation of $S^3$ with twelve vertices in which every edge is contained in a square; this proves Milizia's Conjecture~6.31. We also prove a general criterion for the tangent Euler class of a Davis $4$-manifold to be bounded, and we verify it for $T_{12}$ by means of an explicit symmetric form. Since the Euler class takes the value $256$ on the fundamental class of $M(T_{12})$, the duality between bounded cohomology and simplicial volume gives $\|M(T_{12})\|>0$. This answers Milizia's Question~1.7.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Lai, Xueyuan Wan

item.title: Floer lasagna modules for some 2-handlebodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.34744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Morrison, Walker and Wedrich used Khovanov homology to define the skein lasagna module for a 4-manifold with a link in its boundary. The skein lasagna module was shown to be a deep and powerful invariant; in particular, Ren and Willis proved that it detects exotic smooth structures. Still, computing the skein lasagna module outside some carefully chosen grading range remains an important open problem. Motivated by this construction, Chen defined the Floer lasagna module using Heegaard Floer link homology. In this paper, we give a complete, but partially conjectural description of Floer lasagna modules for a class of 4-manifolds obtained by adding 2-handles along plumbed L-space knots (with certain framing constraints). In particular, we prove that for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ it is infinite-dimensional, and conjecture that for $\mathbb{CP}^2$ it is infinite-dimensional as well. We compute this module for $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ (and conjecturally for $\mathbb{CP}^2$) in all Alexander and Maslov gradings. This strengthens and extends the recent results of McCulloch.
item.dc:creator: Akram Alishahi, Eugene Gorsky, Beibei Liu

item.title: The Alexander polynomial of twisted torus knots in the complementary range
item.description: arXiv:2610.34813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A twisted torus knot T(p,q;r,s) is obtained from the flat-torus diagram of T(p,q) by inserting s full twists along a disk meeting r adjacent strands. Our previous work determined its Alexander polynomial for 1<r<=max{|p|,|q|}. In this paper, we compute it in the complementary range max{|p|,|q|}<r<=|p|+|q| by placing the knot on a standard genus-two Heegaard surface and applying Fox calculus. We then combine the two calculations into a unified Alexander-polynomial formula valid for 1<r<=|p|+|q|. In the complementary range, we prove monicity and give an explicit formula for the breadth. This determines the Seifert genus for nonnegative twists and gives a genus lower bound for negative twists. We also exhibit infinite two-parameter families of non-L-space knots in the complementary range.
item.dc:creator: Adnan, Kyungbae Park

item.title: A lifting defect for oriented $t_3$ and $\bar t_6$ moves
item.description: arXiv:2610.34831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study oriented $t_3$- and $\bar t_6$-moves through the problem of lifting Fox $3$-colorings to colorings by a nine-element Alexander quandle. We define a nonnegative integer lifting defect $\delta$ for oriented links and prove that it is invariant under these moves. For knots, the defect equals the rank of an alternating bilinear form obtained from a Seifert matrix, so it is even. We also prove that it is additive under connected sum. Let $K_s$ be the connected sum of $s\geq 1$ copies of $9_{46}$. Then $\delta(K_s)=2s$, so these knots represent infinitely many distinct equivalence classes under the oriented moves, and none is equivalent to an unlink. After forgetting orientation, each $K_s$ can be transformed into an unlink with $2s+1$ components by $3s$ ordinary $3$-moves.
item.dc:creator: Wenbiao Liu

item.title: On a family of stably handle-slide trivial R-links
item.description: arXiv:2610.35120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An R-link is an n-component link L in S^3 such that Dehn surgery on L yields #^nS1 \times S2. Adapting work of Gompf, Scharlemann and Thompson, Meier and Zupan produced a family of R-links L(p, q; c/d), where the pairs (p, q) and (c, d) are relatively prime and c is even. For most of link in this family, whether it is handle-slide trivial remains open. In this work, we show one subfamily, L(3, 2; 4/d), are stably handle-slide trivial for all d.
item.dc:creator: Wenjie Diao

item.title: Knot Floer complexes of generalized L-space knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.35305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study height 4 knots, which generalize L-space knots and almost L-space knots studied by Ozsv\'ath--Szab\'o, Baldwin--Sivek, and Binns. A knot $K\subset S^3$ is called a height $m$ knot if $\operatorname{rank} \widehat{HF}(S^3_n(K))-n=m$ for all integers $n\geq 2g(K)-1$, where $\widehat{HF}$ is the hat version of Heegaard Floer homology introduced by Ozsv\'ath--Szab\'o. In particular, height 0 and height 2 knots are exactly L-space knots and almost L-space knots, respectively. We prove that the knot Floer complex $CFK^\infty(S^3,K)$ of a height 4 knot $K$ admits a basis that is horizontally and vertically simplified--an hv-basis for short. Moreover, we show that under such an hv-basis, the horizontal and vertical differentials fall into six cases, generalizing the results for L-space knots and almost L-space knots. The hv-basis of the knot Floer complex of $K$ can determine, via an explicit algorithm, the immersed curve of Hanselman-Rasmussen-Watson for the knot complement of $K$. Consequently, our results facilitate further exploration of computations of $\widehat{HF}$ for the gluing of two height 4 knot complements.
item.dc:creator: Shengyu Zou

item.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
item.description: arXiv:2610.35534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elhamdadi, Bryce Virgin

item.title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.33344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets. We derive recurrence relations and partial differential equations for the corresponding bivariate generating functions. In this setting, we obtain recurrences for connected configurations and explicit coefficient formulas for possibly disconnected configurations, both with and without a distinguished initial complex.
item.dc:creator: Ali Aliev, Natalia Amburg

item.title: Volume of area-bounded PGL3-Hitchin moduli space
item.description: arXiv:2610.33417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the $\mathrm{PGL}_3$-Hitchin moduli space of unmarked convex $\mathbb{RP}^2$ structures on the surface $S_{g,m}$ with fixed boundary data $\mathbf L$ when $m>0$, we investigate the subset whose canonical Hilbert--Busemann area is bounded above by $t$. We show that the Goldman symplectic volume of this subset is at most $C_{g,m}(t+\lambda^2)^{8g-8+3m}$, where $\lambda$ is the largest total-root boundary length for $m>0$ and is set to $0$ for $m=0$. As a consequence, We obtain the explicit upper bound for the $e^{-s\cdot\mathrm{Area}}$-weighted volume.
item.dc:creator: Qiongling Li, Beibei Liu, Weixu Su, Zhe Sun

item.title: Aspherical Symplectic Manifolds with Positive First Chern Degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.34998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every integer $n\ge5$, we construct a closed aspherical symplectic manifold of real dimension $2n$ with positive first Chern degree. Each example is a flat torus bundle over the same compact hyperbolic surface, with arithmetic monodromy arising from an explicit indefinite quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$. We identify its symplectic first Chern class with the pullback of the canonical class of the base and compute its degree explicitly. Asphericity rules out nonconstant pseudoholomorphic spheres for every tame almost complex structure. Thus these examples give a negative answer to the symplectic uniruledness question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell in every even real dimension at least ten.
item.dc:creator: Jingcao Wu

item.title: Non-discrete complex hyperbolic $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$-triangle groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.35197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study complex hyperbolic triangle groups of type $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$ with $3\le p_1\le p_2\le p_3\le p_4\le \infty$. We show that if the element $R_1R_2R_3$ is elliptic, then the group is either non-discrete or it belongs to a short list of known discrete groups.
item.dc:creator: Wei Liao, John R Parker

item.title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings
item.description: arXiv:2610.35222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Capovilla, Alberto Casali, Marco Moraschini

item.title: The Weyl Problem for Planar CBB$(-1)$ Surfaces in Hyperbolic $3$-Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the Weyl problem for noncompact convex surfaces in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. We prove that any planar CBB$(-1)$ surface with countably many ends can be isometrically embedded as the boundary of a closed convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{H}^3$ such that each connected component of the ideal boundary of $X$ is either a round disk or a single point. By known rigidity results, such an embedding is unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, we show that the assumption of countably many ends can be dropped if Koebe's circle domain conjecture holds.
item.dc:creator: Xinrong Zhao

item.title: Handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves
item.description: arXiv:2306.10519v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The complement of plane algebraic curves are well studied from topological and algebro-geometric viewpoints. In this paper, we will describe the explicit handle decompositions and the Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves. The method is based on the notion of braid monodromy. We refined this technique to obtain handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Sakumi Sugawara

item.title: Every $S^2$-Bundle over a positive genus($g>1$) Surface has Mapping Class Group of Infinite Rank
item.description: arXiv:2509.16520v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2025, Lin, Wu, Xie and Zhang extend Dax invariant from embedded disks to embedded surfaces and show that there is surjective homomorphism from $MCG(M)$ to $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$ for $M= \Sigma \times S^2$. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed surface with positive$(g>1)$ genus, in the paper we show that for any nontrivial $S^2$ fiber bundles $X= \Sigma \ltimes S^2$, whether $X$ orientable or nonorientable, there is a surjective homomorphism from $MCG(X)$ to $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$. The proof is an application of generalization of Dax invariants for embedded surfaces and the restriction on pseudo-isotopy subgroup $MCG_0(X)$ also surjects on $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$. The property of $MCG(X)$ inherits from trivial fiber bundle $\Sigma \times S^2$ and main theorem shows that the algebraic size of the smooth mapping class group of $S^2$-fiber bundles does not depend on the triviality of the bundle.
item.dc:creator: Huizheng Guo

item.title: Free maps in critical dimension on low-dimensional tori and closed surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.24610v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a method to build free immersions in critical dimension on $m$-tori for $m = 2, 3, 4, 5$ by using a factorization trick inspired by tori immersions in critical dimension. As an application, we show that the set of smooth free maps from a closed surface $M$ to $\mathbb R^5$ is nonempty. In particular, every closed surface embeds freely in $\mathbb R^5$. Finally, we find the homotopy invariants of free maps in our environment and study which invariants are achieved by our maps.
item.dc:creator: Roberto De Leo

item.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
item.description: arXiv:2609.24834v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.
item.dc:creator: Zuyi Zhang

item.title: Plane separating continua inscribe rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2609.25574v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the following: If $X$ is a plane separating continuum, then every embedding of $X$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the vertices of a Euclidean rectangle. We arrive to this result by extending a known result by H. Vaughan for Jordan curves to a wider class of topological objects via shape theory and Steenrod homology.
item.dc:creator: Ulises Morales-Fuentes, Cristina Villanueva-Segovia

item.title: On the closure of irregular orbits of the horocyclic flow on infinite finness
item.description: arXiv:2504.20274v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The topological dynamics of the horocyclic flow h_R on the unit tangent bundle of a geometrically finite hyperbolic surface is well known. In particular on such a surface the flow h_R is minimal or the minimal sets are the periodic orbits. When the surface is geometrically infinite, the situation is more complex and the presence of possible irregular orbits makes the description of minimal sets complicated. In this text, we construct a family of infinite hyperbolic surfaces for which the horocyclic flow defined on the unit tangent bundle is not minimal.
item.dc:creator: Amadou Sy, Masseye Gaye

item.title: Lie structures in homotopy and isotopy calculi
item.description: arXiv:2505.01375v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish compatibility of Lie structures that appear in homotopy calculus of functors and isotopy calculus of embeddings. On one hand, we give a new proof of the Johnson--Arone--Mahowald result describing the layers of the Goodwillie tower of the identity functor, and we directly compare the spectral Lie bracket with the classical Whitehead bracket on spaces. On the other hand, we geometrically define a bracket on the layers of the embedding calculus tower for embeddings of arcs. These results are unified through the same technical tool, a newly defined bracket on total homotopy fibres of collapsing cubes of wedge sums.
item.dc:creator: Danica Kosanovi\'c

item.title: On smooth and bundle structures on topological manifolds homotopy equivalent to $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.16307v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We first verify the expected calculations of the topological structure set, in the sense of surgery theory, for the total spaces of $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$ for $k\ge3$, in which manifolds homotopy equivalent to the total spaces are organized. Next, we investigate the question of which of the elements in these structure sets can be realized as such bundles. Moreover, we study the forgetful map from the smooth version to the topological version of the structure set; we determine its image. All elements in the image turn out to have the underlying manifold such a bundle.
item.dc:creator: Ajay Raj, Tibor Macko

item.title: Non-maximal quasi-isometric $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$-representations via alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.24672v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every admissible non-maximal Toledo invariant $t$, we construct a locus of irreducible representations of a closed genus-$g$ surface group into $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$ with Toledo invariant $t$ whose orbit maps are quasi-isometric embeddings. These loci have real codimension $10(g-1)$ or $10(g-1)+2(n-1)$ in the character variety depending on the Toledo value. Our construction uses $4$-cyclic Higgs bundles and their correspondence with $\partial$-alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces. The associated equivariant minimal maps into the symmetric space are bi-Lipschitz embeddings. We further construct cocompact domains of discontinuity in the Shilov boundary. Their quotients are smooth fiber bundles over the surface with fiber homeomorphic to $S^{2n-1}\times S^{2n-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Qiongling Li, Junming Zhang

item.title: Robert J. Daverman (1941-2026)
item.description: arXiv:2609.28515v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is an expanded version of a memorial article that is to appear in the Notices of the American Mathematical Society.
item.dc:creator: Gerard Venema, Craig Guilbault

item.title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28531v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $\delta^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{\delta+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,\Delta}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $\Delta(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $\delta+1={\rm deg}\,\Delta$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.
item.dc:creator: Ya. Kononov, A. Morozov
